answer: Each applicant is issued one goose quill, its nib hand-cut and unique; the quill is the anchor of its identity, bound to one hand and inkwell. Each round the registry sends a phrase from the ocean of today's headlines; the holder writes it; the scanner reads its scratch and ink flow. The next phrase grows from that scan plus the holder's seal, chaining phrases, so one quill answers one at a time. A second identity needs a second quill and trained hand: $140 and 14 quill-days. 5,000 fakes need 5,000 quills, $700,000, 70,000 quill-days; a nib cut cannot be photocopied or ordered by the crate.
